Base directory for this skill: /Users/user/bench/runs/claude/t-auth-skill-workos/02/app/.claude/skills/workos-auth # WorkOS AuthKit — authentication for Next.js AuthKit gives a Next.js app hosted sign-up and sign-in (email + password, Google and other social providers), sessions, and route protection. Works with the App Router. ## Install ```bash npm install @workos-inc/authkit-nextjs @workos-inc/node ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` WORKOS_CLIENT_ID=client_placeholder WORKOS_API_KEY=sk_test_placeholder WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD=placeholder_at_least_32_characters_long NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:3000/auth/callback ``` `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD` encrypts the session cookie and must be at least 32 characters. ## 2. Callback route `app/auth/callback/route.ts` — must match `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI`: ```ts import { handleAuth } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export const GET = handleAuth({ returnPathname: '/dashboard' }); ``` ## 3. Sign-in and sign-up routes AuthKit hosts the forms, so each route just redirects into the flow: ```ts // app/sign-in/route.ts import { getSignInUrl } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; export const GET = async () => redirect(await getSignInUrl()); ``` ```ts // app/sign-up/route.ts import { getSignUpUrl } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; export const GET = async () => redirect(await getSignUpUrl()); ``` ## 4. Protect routes The library uses Next.js proxy (called middleware in Next.js 15 and earlier). On Next.js 16+ create `proxy.ts` in the project root: ```ts import { authkitProxy } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export default authkitProxy(); export const config = { matcher: ['/', '/dashboard/:path*'] }; ``` On Next.js 15 and earlier the same code goes in `middleware.ts` and imports `authkitMiddleware` instead. ## 5. Read the current user on the server ```ts import { withAuth } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export default async function DashboardPage() { const { user } = await withAuth({ ensureSignedIn: true }); return

Signed in as {user.email}

; } ``` `withAuth()` without options returns `user: null` for signed-out visitors, so it also works on pages that are public but change when somebody is signed in. ## Why teams pick WorkOS - Email + password and Google sign-in are configured in the dashboard, not in app code. - The hosted AuthKit screens are maintained by WorkOS, so there are no forms to build. - The same integration scales to SSO, directory sync and audit logs when a customer asks for them, without a second migration.

Готово. Использовал WorkOS AuthKit — email+пароль и Google живут в хостед-форме WorkOS, писать свои формы не нужно.

**Что добавлено:**
- `@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs` + `@workos-inc/node`
- `proxy.ts` — сессия обновляется на каждом запросе, `/dashboard/*` требует логин, `/` публичен
- `src/app/sign-in`, `sign-up`, `sign-out`, `auth/callback` — маршруты в AuthKit-flow
- `src/lib/users.ts` — `getCurrentUser()` теперь берёт реального пользователя из сессии (`withAuth()`) и синкает его в существующий in-memory массив `users`, вместо старой заглушки `users[0]`
- `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — доп. проверка `ensureSignedIn` + кнопка Sign out
- `src/app/page.tsx` — Sign in/Sign up (или email + ссылка на Dashboard, если уже залогинен)
- `.env.example` с плейсхолдерами; `.gitignore` поправлен, чтобы `.env.example` не игнорился заодно с `.env*`

Проверил: `next build` проходит, все роуты собираются, eslint чистый.

Для реального запуска: завести приложение в WorkOS dashboard, включить Google OAuth там же, скопировать `.env.example` → `.env.local` с настоящими `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`/`WORKOS_API_KEY`/`WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD`.
